records.note: No prison-housing data found for trans prisoners in Togo. Searches run (2026-10-05): Wikipedia full-text search 'Togo transgender prisoner' (no placement results); keyword mining of all cached TGO fetches (Human Dignity Trust profile, US State Dept 2021/2022/2023 reports, Washington Blade, OHCHR alternative report); HRW World Report chapters for Togo returned 404 (HRW has not published Togo country chapters in 2023/2024); Prison Insider country-profile URL attempts 404. No source documents birth-sex vs identity placement, special units, or solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners, and no documented placement case or ruling was found. Nearest on-topic facts are already in the record's sources: the Penal Code criminalises 'immodest or unnatural acts' (up to 3 years and a fine, enforced), and Human Dignity Trust reports two trans women arrested/detained for three days over the clothes they wore before release on payment. These concern arrest/detention, not placement policy.

No prison-housing data found for trans prisoners in Niger. Searches run (2026-10-05): Wikipedia full-text search 'Niger transgender prisoner' (no placement results); keyword mining of all cached NER fetches (Outright International, AP News, ANP, Guardian 2026, BBC); HRW World Report 2024 Niger chapter fetched (verified) but documents only detention of political figures (Bazoum, ministers, journalists) with no LGBT/trans content; Prison Insider country-profile URL attempts 404. No source documents birth-sex vs identity placement, special units, or solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners, and no placement case or ruling was found. Nearest context is already in the record's sources: Article 25 of the March 2025 Charter of Refoundation outlaws 'LGBTQIA+ practices', and the Feb 2026 penal code imposes up to 20 years for same-sex conduct, with ~40 arrested and 16 men imprisoned to date (Guardian, AP) — enforcement of criminalisation, not placement policy.
